messages.subject: select a certain set of pixels for "MSImageSet"
messages.subject_clean: select a certain set of pixels for "MSImageSet"
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

Thank you very much for creating Cardinal, I find it extremely useful for my work.
I am trying to do clustering on my MSI data. Here is the workflow:

HG <- "human_G"
folder <- "/Users/olgagavrilenko/Desktop/ImzML"
data_HG <- readImzML(HG, folder, mass.range = c(500,1000),  as="MSImageSet")
norm_HG <- normalize(data_HG, method="tic")
norm_HG <- norm_HG[,!duplicated(coord(norm_HG))]
peaklist.HG <- peakPick(norm_HG, method = "simple")
HG.ssca<- spatialShrunkenCentroids(peaklist.HG, r=c(1,2), k=c(10,15), s = c(0,1), algorithm="Lloyd", method = "gaussian" )

The image I get then by calling an image() function is in the attached. With a black line I indicated the boundaries of my actual sample. The rest, as I suppose, is the MALDI matrix or something else. Are there possible ways to remove it?

I have tried setting the number of clusters to 2, and then the data clusters to two items: the sample, and the matrix (or whatever behind the boundaries of the sample). Is it anyhow possible to select the pixels that only belong to the sample and "feed" them again to the clustering algorithm?

I hope my explanations are not very confusing.
Thank you in advance!

Best,
Olga

messages.subject_clean: select a certain set of pixels for "MSImageSet"
messages.body_plain:
You can subset by accessing the pixel-wise k cluster values, see below.
#run analysis
ssc_out <- spatialShrunkenCentroids(d, r=1, k=10,s=1)

#look for a certain set of k cluster
cluster_indices <- c(1,2,4)

#boolean vector for each pixel where TRUE means it is the cluster
#since you are running multiple models, you will need to select the right one
#after ssc_out$classes$'my good model'
pixels_in_cluster <- ssc_out$classes$`r = 1, k = 10, s = 1` %in% cluster_indices

#slice original IMS data
d_subset <- d[,pixels_in_cluster]

The generated data will just be a new Cardinal MSImageSet.

Heath

messages.subject: Re: Indexing samples in merged data
messages.body_plain:
The entire data structure can be indexed like a matrix, where rows are features (m/z features) and columns are pixels (spectra).

For example, if you are working with MSImageSet:

s1 <- pData(mydata)$sample == "sample1"
mydata_sample1 <- mydata[,s1]

or if you are working with MSImagingExperiment:

s1 <- run(mydata) == "sample1"
mydata_sample1 <- mydata[,s1]

messages.subject_clean: Consensus peaks from 'processed' data in sparse mat
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kylie,

I'm wondering if I'm missing something in processed data in Cardinal. I have sets of peak lists (essentially processed imaging data) where I've built a ProcessedMSImagingExperiment with a ppm of 3 as the data has decent mass resolution. In this case, the summary looks like this:

An object of class 'MSProcessedImagingExperiment'
  <267858 feature, 10000 pixel> imaging dataset
    imageData(1): intensity
    featureData(0):
    pixelData(0):
    run(1): test
    raster dimensions: 397 x 26
    coord(2): x = 2600..2996, y = 874..899
    mass range:  294.000 to 2505.982
    centroided: TRUE

There are 267,858 mass bins, almost all of these are noise, have intensity values very close to zero if we summarize by mean, or are empty. Is there an efficient way to reduce the dimension by intensity threshold, frequency filtering, or some other operation to arrive at a representative consensus m/z list that is much smaller and amenable to a not-processed version of the data? Probably the true number of peaks in this dataset is around 3000-5000. Thanks for any advice you may have.

Heath

The segmentation is driven by the data, and sometimes may not exactly reflect visible morphological structures.

You can certainly subset the data to the peaks you wish to use, if you want to create a segmentation from a manually-selected subset of peaks. Just give the method the subsetted dataset.
